messages:
Elliot Price: We need to lock down docs IA + URLs for the generated model release notes before we merge the build step. Current PR draft assumes a `/release-notes/models/...` tree but I want to sanity check with Product + Console folks.

Wei Chen: +1. Biggest questions for me:
1) canonical model identifier vs display name
2) where versioned pages live (and what the “latest” alias is)
3) how this ties into the model catalog pages (which today are basically “overview” pages)

Kira Thompson: Also: Private customers will ask “where do I find the release notes I got in the upgrade bundle?” We probably need a stable URL pattern we can reference in Private docs even if the actual content is generated.

Kenji Nakamura: From UX side, I’d prefer:
- model catalog page stays stable (per model)
- release notes are a tab/section on that page OR a predictable “Release notes” subpage
- deep links to a specific version should be shareable.

Jada Williams: FWIW the generator artifact format we’re standardizing has:
- `model_slug`
- `variant` / `profile` (e.g. `fp16`, `int8`)
- `version` (semver)
- `deployment_availability` (hosted/dedicated/private)
Docs can ignore some of that, but Console will show filtered views.

Wei Chen: The thing I’m worried about is slugs. We already have names like “Llama 3 70B Instruct” in marketing docs. We need the URL to use the registry slug, not the pretty name.

Elliot Price: Agreed. Proposal:
- Canonical slug = model registry `model_slug` (kebab-case)
- Model catalog page: `/models/{model_slug}/`
- Release notes index: `/models/{model_slug}/release-notes/`
- Specific version: `/models/{model_slug}/release-notes/{version}/`

Kira Thompson: That would be super clean. What about variants (quantization profiles)? Do we need a dimension in the URL?

Jada Williams: Variants are tricky. Most customers think in terms of “the model” and only sometimes in terms of quantization profile.
Internally the change events are per “served model id” (model + profile). If docs only publishes per model, we risk mixing unrelated changes.

Felix Schneider: Console will likely show “Llama-3-70B-Instruct (fp16)” vs “(int8)” as separate rows when browsing history. For docs, we could collapse by default but allow filtering.

Wei Chen: If we collapse, we need a disclosure on the page. Otherwise people will copy/paste a release note that only applied to int8 and assume fp16 changed.

Kenji Nakamura: Can we add a query param for profile? Like:
`/models/{slug}/release-notes/{version}/?profile=int8`
But canonical URL stays profile-less.

Jada Williams: Generator can emit both:
- model-level entry (aggregated)
- profile-level entries (separate)
But MVP is probably profile-level only; aggregation is extra logic and more redaction risk.

Connor O'Brien: Jumping in — release engineering preference is “1 artifact -> 1 page”. If generator outputs profile-level entries, docs should map 1:1 to avoid clever grouping.
We can add an index page that lists all profiles under a model.

Elliot Price: That makes sense. Updated URL plan:
- Model page: `/models/{model_slug}/`
- Release notes landing: `/models/{model_slug}/release-notes/`
- Profile landing: `/models/{model_slug}/release-notes/{profile_slug}/` (e.g. `fp16`, `int8`, `awq-int4`)
- Version page: `/models/{model_slug}/release-notes/{profile_slug}/{version}/`

Wei Chen: +1. And the model page can link to the release notes landing. On landing, show profiles + latest version for each.

Kira Thompson: For Private docs, we can say “see release notes for the model/profile you deployed” and link to the profile landing. Also aligns with upgrade bundle naming (we already include profile in the bundle).

Kenji Nakamura: Works for IA. We can present it as:
- Release notes (choose a deployment profile)
Then list versions w/ filters.

Felix Schneider: What about “latest” shortcut? People will type it.

Wei Chen: Please no “latest” as a hard canonical path for version pages (SEO + caching headaches). But we can have a redirect:
`/models/{slug}/release-notes/{profile}/latest/` -> resolves to current latest version.

Elliot Price: +1 redirect only. Canonical should always be `/.../{version}/`.

Jada Williams: Also note: deprecations. A deprecated version might still exist for pinned customers. Pages should remain accessible even after deprecation.

Wei Chen: Yes, and we should keep an “End of support” banner on the version page if `deprecation.status != active`.

Kira Thompson: Another thing: embargoed / customer-specific notes. We can’t publish those publicly.

Elliot Price: Docs build will only consume the PUBLIC changelog artifacts (post-redaction). Anything internal-only should never land in `redwood-docs` repo build inputs.

Connor O'Brien: That’s consistent with CI gate: generator emits 2 artifacts (public + internal). Docs only reads public, Console reads both with RBAC.

Wei Chen: Can we also generate a JSON feed for the release notes landing pages? Customers ask for machine readable.

Elliot Price: PR-9312 includes RSS + JSON feed at:
- `/release-notes/models/feed.xml` (global)
- `/release-notes/models/feed.json` (global)
But with new IA, should become:
- `/models/release-notes/feed.xml`
- `/models/release-notes/feed.json`
And potentially per-model feed:
- `/models/{slug}/release-notes/feed.json`

Jada Williams: Generator can support “list recent changes by model_slug”. Docs can expose that as per-model feeds later. MVP global feed is fine.

Kenji Nakamura: UX note: global feed is ok but we should also have a “Release notes” index page in docs nav. Otherwise discoverability is rough.

Wei Chen: IA proposal for nav:
Docs > Models > (Model Catalog)
Docs > Release notes > Models
Then inside each model page: link to release notes.

Elliot Price: Sounds good. Action items:
- I’ll update docs IA + routes in PR-9312 to use `/models/{slug}/release-notes/{profile}/{version}/`
- Wei: draft microcopy + banners (deprecated, breaking change)
- Jada: confirm profile_slug list comes from metadata and is stable
- Connor: confirm redirect strategy for `/latest/` is acceptable w/ release eng

docs-bot: buildkite: `redwood-docs` pipeline #1841 succeeded (preview deployed): https://preview.docs.redwoodinference.dev/pr-9312/

Wei Chen: Preview looks good. Only nit: the profile slug currently renders as `awq_int4` (underscore) in breadcrumb. Can we normalize to kebab?

Jada Williams: Yes. Schema defines `profile_id` as `[a-z0-9-]+`. If you’re seeing underscore, it’s coming from old records. Migration should normalize, but docs should be defensive and kebab-case it on render.

Elliot Price: Great — we’ll normalize on render and file a follow-up to ensure registry backfill enforces it.

Kira Thompson: +1. This will save us from broken links in Private docs.

Connor O'Brien: Redirect plan ok. We’ll treat `/latest/` as a convenience alias, not a contract for offline bundles.

Elliot Price: Cool. I’ll post an update in the PR and link this thread for the record.
